title: The Khalsa and the Five Ks
objective: After this level you can explain why Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa in 1699 and what the Five Ks mean to Sikhs who wear them.
summary: After his father's execution in 1675, Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa in 1699: a casteless order of initiated Sikhs who take the names Singh and Kaur and wear the Five Ks as articles of faith.

cards.headline: A plain steel bracelet can be a promise.
cards.body: For initiated Sikhs, the kara is one of five articles of faith worn every day. All five go back to Baisakhi Day in 1699.

cards.headline: A Guru in hard times
cards.body: Gobind Singh became the tenth Guru in 1675, at nine, after his father, Guru Tegh Bahadur, was executed by the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb. On Baisakhi Day in 1699, at Anandpur in Punjab, he founded the Khalsa: a casteless order of Sikhs committed to courage and to their faith. Those who join are initiated with amrit, sweetened water stirred with a double-edged sword.

cards.headline: Shared names
cards.body: Khalsa men take the name Singh, "lion", and women the name Kaur, "princess". Members also pledge to give up tobacco, alcohol and certain meats. One surname for every man, one for every woman: a casteless order, written into people's names.

cards.headline: The Five Ks
cards.body: Initiated Khalsa Sikhs wear five articles of faith, each beginning with K. Kesh: uncut hair, for belonging. Kara: a steel bracelet, for self-restraint and discipline. Kangha: a comb, for cleanliness. Kirpan: a sword, for self-respect and readiness to face challenges. Kachera: an undergarment, for moral restraint.

cards.headline: The Khalsa and the Five Ks: the takeaways
learned: Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa in 1699
Khalsa men take the name Singh, women Kaur
The Five Ks are articles of faith, each with a meaning

questions.prompt: Which of the Five Ks is a steel bracelet?
questions.explanation: The kara is a steel bracelet, standing for self-restraint and discipline.

questions.prompt: Why did Guru Gobind Singh found the Khalsa in 1699?

options.label: To choose the next human Guru
options.rationale: He ended the line of human Gurus.

options.label: To form a casteless order committed to the faith
To compile the first Sikh scripture
To serve as officials of the Mughal court
options.rationale: The Mughal emperor had executed his father.

questions.explanation: He founded the Khalsa as a casteless order of Sikhs committed to courage and to their faith.

questions.prompt: What links the casteless Khalsa to the langar's single straight line from Level 57?

options.label: Both were founded by Guru Nanak himself
options.rationale: Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa in 1699.

options.label: Both put Sikh equality into practice, against caste
Both began when the Adi Granth was compiled
options.rationale: That was 1604; the Khalsa came in 1699.

questions.explanation: The langar began as a protest against caste, and the Khalsa is a casteless order: two practical forms of equality.
